question: What is the primary function of the respiratory system that gets disrupted during disorders?
explanation: The main job of the respiratory system is moving oxygen into the blood and removing carbon dioxide. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why do patients experience shortness of breath when they have a respiratory problem?

options.A: The kidneys are retaining too much water
options.B: The heart is pumping too much blood to the muscles
options.C: The stomach is pushing upward against the diaphragm
options.D: The body is trying to fix low oxygen or high carbon dioxide levels

explanation: Think of shortness of breath as an alarm bell! It's your body's clever way of telling you it needs more oxygen or needs to blow off extra carbon dioxide. Great effort!

question: What term is used to describe shortness of breath that occurs specifically when a patient lies flat?
explanation: Orthopnea is breathing difficulty that worsens when lying down and improves when sitting upright. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h2)

question: A patient wakes up gasping for air two hours after falling asleep and has to sit by the window to breathe. What is this called?
explanation: You're doing great! Waking up suddenly in the middle of the night feeling starved for air is known as paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (PND). It's a classic sign often seen in heart issues.

question: What does a rust-colored sputum sample often point toward?
explanation: Rust-colored sputum contains blood mixed with inflammatory exudate, which is typical of pneumococcal pneumonia. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h3)

question: Why is pink and frothy sputum an urgent sign that nurses must report immediately?

options.A: It is a normal byproduct of taking cough syrup
options.B: It means the patient is swallowing too much saliva
options.C: It indicates fluid backing up into the air sacs from the heart
options.D: It shows the patient has been smoking too many cigarettes

explanation: Well done! Pink and frothy sputum tells us fluid is leaking into the tiny air sacs in the lungs (pulmonary edema)—definitely something you want to catch and report fast!

question: What is the medical term for coughing up blood from the lungs?
explanation: Hemoptysis refers specifically to blood that comes up from the respiratory system through coughing. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h4)

question: Why do many lung diseases cause sharp chest pain only when the patient takes a deep breath?

options.A: Air is getting trapped inside the stomach muscles
options.B: The main airway is swelling shut during inhalation
options.C: The heart muscle is stretching too hard against the ribcage
options.D: The inflamed lining of the lungs rubs against the chest wall during movement

explanation: Think of it like a skin scrape rubbing against clothing: when the pleural lining of the lungs gets inflamed, every deep breath causes those sore layers to rub together and hurt!

question: What physical sign involves a bluish color of the skin due to low oxygen in the blood?
explanation: Cyanosis is the bluish tint seen on the skin and lips when deoxygenated hemoglobin levels rise. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h5)

question: Why might a severely anemic patient NOT show a blue skin color (cyanosis) even when their oxygen is dangerously low?

options.A: Their skin is naturally thicker and hides color changes better
options.B: Anemia causes the blood vessels to dilate and turn the skin red instead
options.C: They do not have enough red blood cells or hemoglobin to display the blue color
options.D: Their lungs absorb extra oxygen from the surrounding air

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! Cyanosis needs enough hemoglobin (the stuff in red blood cells that carries oxygen) to show that blue tint. If a patient is severely anemic, they simply don't have enough to show the color!

question: Which breath sound is described as a continuous musical whistle heard when airways are narrowed?
explanation: Wheezes are high-pitched musical sounds created when air flows through constricted bronchial tubes. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h6)

question: A nurse listens with a stethoscope and hears moist, popping sounds at the lung bases of a patient with heart failure. What are these sounds called?
explanation: Great job! Crackles sound just like Velcro pulling apart or bubbles popping, caused by fluid opening up those tiny air sacs.

question: What is finger clubbing typically associated with in chronic conditions?

options.C: Long-term low oxygen levels in the blood
options.D: A temporary lack of dietary vitamins

explanation: Finger clubbing develops gradually as a result of chronic hypoxia and tissue changes in the extremities. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h7)

question: Why do many patients with severe, long-term lung disease experience noticeable weight loss and muscle wasting?

options.A: The physical effort of breathing uses up enormous amounts of energy
options.B: Their digestive tracts stop absorbing nutrients completely
options.C: They deliberately avoid eating to prevent shortness of breath
options.D: Liver damage prevents them from storing body fat

explanation: Think about how hard it is to run a race—now imagine working that hard just to breathe all day! That heavy effort burns massive amounts of energy and leads to weight loss.

question: What is the very FIRST thing a nurse should do when a patient suddenly gets severe shortness of breath?

options.A: Help the patient sit up and check their oxygen delivery
options.B: Leave the room immediately to find the attending doctor
options.C: Document the exact time the symptoms started
options.D: Have the patient lie flat on their back for rest

explanation: Patient comfort and breathing come first! Always help them sit upright and check their oxygen before you start writing notes or running off.

question: Which of the following is NOT helpful to include when charting about a patient's cough?

options.A: Factors that make the coughing worse
options.B: The color and amount of any sputum produced
options.C: The brand of soap used in the hospital room
options.D: Whether the cough is dry or productive

explanation: You got it! The soap brand won't change lung assessment findings, but details about sputum, triggers, and cough type are clinical gold!
